chunk_findings.detail: The severity filter normalizes a missing severity to the empty string (`(r.get("severity") or "").strip().lower()`) but then compares it literally to the requested severity. A bug whose severity is unset (`None` or empty) therefore never matches `severity == "unset"`. Given one open bug with no severity value and `bug list --severity unset`, the predicate evaluates `"" == "unset"` as false, the filtered set becomes empty, and the function returns `O.nothing("view.list", "No bugs with severity unset.")`, even though the new `bug status` surface is required to report that bug in the `unset` severity bucket. The filter must normalize empty severity to `unset` (or otherwise match `unset` to empty) to be consistent with the severity facet/status reporting.

chunk_findings.detail: `bug_status` counts an open bug as blocked whenever its fix task has a non-empty `needs` list. The recorded rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave] says tasks state their dependencies in `needs` (and may inherit phase needs), so `needs` is the declared dependency set, not an indicator that any need is unmet. For example, an open bug with `fix_task="T1"` where `T1.state != BLOCKED` and `T1.needs=["D1"]` with `D1` already met will be counted in `blocked`; then `unblocked=total-blocked-no_fix_task` reports 0 instead of 1. If bug fix tasks carry phase needs as the rule requires, the status can classify every fix-tasked open bug as blocked.

chunk_findings.detail: The test is intended to prove that the MCP severity filter is applied before paging, but it never asserts the page size. It calls `_vl(repo, "bug", limit=1, offset=0)` and then only checks `done.data["total"] == 2` and that every returned row has severity `"high"`. If `_finish_list_read`/`finish_bug_list` filtered by severity but ignored the `limit=1` and returned both high-severity bugs, the assertions would still pass: `total` would be `2` and `{r["severity"] for r in done.data["rows"]}` would still be `{"high"}`. Thus a paging regression after severity filtering would not be caught by this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bug_list.py:test_mcp_severity_filter_is_applied_before_paging

chunk_findings.detail: `_page_from_whole` unconditionally reorders the whole matched bug set with `full.sort(key=lambda r: r["id"])` before paging, even when the caller only asked for a severity filter and did not ask for `sort=severity`. The existing bug-list contract in `finish_bug_list` says the shared engine page is newest-first and that the severity facet should narrow the whole matched set before the page cut, not impose a new ordering. Given a bug list whose newest bug has id `bug-2` and an older bug has id `bug-10`, both with severity `critical`, `bug list --severity critical` (or the MCP equivalent) will sort by id lexicographically and return `bug-10` before `bug-2`, which is wrong because the default page order is supposed to remain newest-first. For numeric-style ids the same line produces oldest-first instead of newest-first, so the returned `rows`, `shown`, `truncated`, and `next` values correspond to the wrong page.

chunk_findings.detail: `bug_status` treats any non-empty `fix.needs` as “blocked,” but the intent says blocked means the fix task has *unmet* needs, and the project rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave] describes `needs` as the task’s stated dependencies, not an unmet-only set. Given an open bug whose fix task has a dependency list such as `needs=["task-1"]` where `task-1` is already done (or even where the fix task itself is done but still carries its dependency list), this branch increments `blocked` and subtracts from `unblocked`, so the command reports the bug as blocked despite having no unmet needs.

chunk_findings.detail: `_unmet` treats `removed` as an unmet dependency condition, but `bug_status` still treats a removed fix task as an existing, unblocked fix task. Given an open bug with `bug.fix_task = "T1"`, `st.items["T1"].removed = True`, `T1.state = "open"`, and `T1.needs = []`, `bug_status` finds `fix is not None`, so it does not increment `no_fix_task`; `_unmet(fix, st)` returns false because the fix task is not terminal, not blocked, and has no needs. The bug is therefore omitted from both `blocked` and `no_fix_task`, so the derived `unblocked = total - blocked - no_fix_task` count incorrectly includes a bug whose fix task has been removed. The dependency branch `d.removed` shows removed items are expected to be retrievable from `st.items`, so the fix-task path needs the same removal check.
